lesson.titleZh: 一個巴掌拍不響／雙方都有責任

examples.en: A: Why are both of them being asked to apologise? B: It takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 甲：為甚麼他們兩個都要道歉？ 乙：一個巴掌拍不響。

examples.en: It takes two to tango, so both partners need to attend the meeting.
examples.zh: 事情需要雙方配合，因此兩名合夥人都需要出席會議。

meaning.en: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.
meaning.zh: 一件涉及兩個人或雙方的事情，通常不能單靠其中一方發生、成功、改善或得到解決。

register.summaryEn: everyday conversation; friendly advice; workplace discussions; interviews; news commentary; general articles; discussions about relationships, teamwork or agreements.
register.summaryZh: it takes two to tango 屬於口語至中性的諺語式表達，常見於日常對話、友善勸告、工作討論、訪問、新聞評論及一般文章。
contextsEn: discussions about relationships, teamwork or agreements
contextsZh: 慣用語前後所交代的具體情境。
register.formalEn: In highly formal academic, legal or technical writing, expressions such as both parties share responsibility or cooperation from both sides is required may be clearer.
register.formalZh: 它與一般動詞短語不同，通常應作為一個完整句子單位記憶及使用：

fixedVariable.fixedEn: Keep the fixed words and word order shown in the source expression.
fixedVariable.fixedZh: 保留原檔目標表達中的固定字詞及字序。

fixedVariable.variableZh: 只按照原檔句式改變動詞形式、所有格、時態或前後文法。

The truth is that it takes two to tango.

specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: it takes two to tango.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：it takes two to tango。

examples.en: A: Why are both of them being asked to apologise? B: It takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 甲：為甚麼他們兩個都要道歉？ 乙：一個巴掌拍不響。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式二：先使用慣用語，再交代結果
specificForms.formula: It takes two to tango, so + result.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The phrase after so is an optional result. It is not part of the fixed expression.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 後面的內容只是補充結果，並不是固定慣用語的一部分。

examples.en: It takes two to tango, so both partners need to attend the meeting.
examples.zh: 事情需要雙方配合，因此兩名合夥人都需要出席會議。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式三：先交代情況，再使用慣用語
specificForms.formula: Situation + ; / — + it takes two to tango.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The semicolon or dash connects the specific situation with the idiomatic conclusion.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 分號或破折號把具體情境與慣用語總結連接起來。

examples.en: Nora cannot repair the friendship alone—it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 諾拉無法獨力修補這段友誼；這需要雙方共同努力。

examples.en: Neither side should place all the blame on the other; it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 任何一方都不應把所有責任推給另一方；一個巴掌拍不響。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式四：置於話語標記之後
specificForms.formula: After all, it takes two to tango.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The opening expression is optional. It helps show how the speaker is presenting the point.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 開首的話語標記屬於可選部分，用來顯示說話者如何提出這個觀點。

examples.en: As everyone knows, it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 大家都知道，事情需要雙方配合。

examples.en: Put simply, it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 簡單來說，雙方都需要參與。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式五：置於 that 之後
specificForms.formula: Subject + reporting or reminder verb + that + it takes two to tango.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The word that belongs to the surrounding clause. It is not part of the fixed idiom.
specificForms.descriptionZh: that 屬於外圍句子結構，並不是固定慣用語的一部分。

examples.en: The manager reminded them that it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 經理提醒他們，事情需要雙方配合。

examples.en: The adviser explained that it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 顧問解釋，協議需要雙方共同努力。

examples.en: Remember that it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 記住，一個巴掌拍不響。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式六：配合引導觀點的子句
specificForms.descriptionEn: These clauses introduce the expression as an important conclusion.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這些子句把目標表達作為重要結論引出。

examples.en: The truth is that it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 事實是，單靠一方並不足夠。

examples.en: The lesson is simple: it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 道理很簡單：一個巴掌拍不響。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式七：先指出適用範圍
specificForms.formula: In + situation, it takes two to tango.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The opening phrase shows which situation the saying applies to.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 開首短語指出這個表達適用於哪一種情況。

examples.en: In a shared project, it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 在共同項目中，事情需要雙方配合。

examples.en: When it comes to rebuilding trust, it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 要重新建立信任，雙方都需要付出努力。

specificForms.formula: Because / Since + it takes two to tango, + result.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Because and since are optional conjunctions outside the fixed expression.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 及 since 是固定表達以外的連接詞。

examples.en: Because it takes two to tango, both players should apologise.
examples.zh: 因為一個巴掌拍不響，兩名球員都應該道歉。

examples.en: Since it takes two to tango, neither team should expect the other to do everything.
examples.zh: 既然事情需要雙方配合，任何一隊都不應期望另一隊完成所有工作。

specificForms.formula: “It takes two to tango,” + speaker + said.
specificForms.descriptionEn: as a complete quotation; after a speaker’s first statement; inside a longer response; after a reporting clause.

examples.en: “It takes two to tango,” the coach reminded the players.
examples.zh: 教練提醒球員：「一個巴掌拍不響。」

specificForms.formula: 2. It takes two to tango, so + result.
specificForms.descriptionEn: This frame explicitly presents the expression as a familiar saying.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這個句式清楚表明說話者正在引用一句常見諺語。

examples.en: It takes two to tango; Leo should not place all the blame on Sara for their argument.
examples.zh: 一個巴掌拍不響；里奧不應把爭吵的全部責任推給莎拉。

benefits.titleZh: 拒絕不公平的單方面歸咎
benefits.en: The idiomatic version gives a compact and memorable response to one-sided blame.
benefits.zh: 里奧不應只責怪莎拉； 一個巴掌拍不響。 慣用語版本能以簡潔而容易記憶的方式反駁單方面歸咎。

examples.en: Leo should not blame only Sara—it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 里奧不應只責怪莎拉；一個巴掌拍不響。

benefits.titleEn: It Explains Why One Person’s Effort Is Not Enough
benefits.titleZh: 解釋為甚麼單靠一方並不足夠
benefits.en: The expression is useful when a relationship, agreement or shared project requires cooperation.
benefits.zh: 諾拉無法獨力修補友誼； 這需要雙方共同努力。 當關係、協議或共同項目需要合作時，這個表達十分實用。

examples.en: Nora cannot repair the friendship alone—it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 諾拉無法獨力修補友誼；這需要雙方共同努力。

benefits.titleEn: It Gives Advice Without a Long Explanation
benefits.en: It Gives Advice Without a Long Explanation
benefits.zh: 不要再互相指責了。 一個巴掌拍不響。

benefits.titleEn: It Works Naturally as a Response
benefits.en: The expression allows the speaker to respond without building a long sentence from the beginning.
benefits.zh: 這個表達讓說話者無須每次由零開始組織一個很長的句子。

benefits.en: The saying can move a discussion away from blame and towards shared action.
benefits.zh: 這句話可以把討論由互相指責轉向共同採取行動。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Summarise a Complicated Situation
benefits.en: The expression packages the ideas of two-sided involvement, shared responsibility and mutual participation into one familiar sentence.
benefits.zh: 道理很簡單：一個巴掌拍不響。 這個表達把雙方參與、共同責任及互相配合等意思濃縮成一句常見說法。

examples.en: The lesson is simple: it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 道理很簡單：一個巴掌拍不響。

origin.statusEn: Well-Documented Popularisation; Exact Earlier Development Uncertain
origin.statusZh: 普及過程有較充分記錄；更早期的確切演變仍未完全確定

history.en: The wording became widely known through the 1952 American song “Takes Two to Tango”, written by Al Hoffman and Dick Manning. Pearl Bailey recorded a successful version, and Louis Armstrong also performed the song. Merriam-Webster connects the familiar expression with this 1952 song and explains that its sound pattern helped make it memorable.
history.zh: 這個說法因1952年的美國歌曲《Takes Two to Tango》而廣為人知。 歌曲由 Al Hoffman 及 Dick Manning 創作，Pearl Bailey 錄製了廣受歡迎的版本，Louis Armstrong 亦曾演唱。

history.en: The dance image was soon extended beyond romance and dancing. Speakers began using it for any situation in which two people or groups had to participate, cooperate or share responsibility.
history.zh: 探戈的雙人舞畫面很快被延伸至愛情及舞蹈以外的情況。 人們開始用它形容任何需要兩個人或兩個群體參與、合作或共同承擔責任的事情。

origin.memoryEn: A partner dance cannot work through one dancer alone; a two-sided situation cannot work through only one side.
origin.memoryZh: 雙人舞不能單靠一名舞者完成；涉及雙方的事情也不能只靠其中一方。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：保持完整子句不變
rules.en: Do not change takes according to another person or subject. The expression already has its fixed subject it.
rules.zh: 不要因其他人物或主語而改變 takes。 這個表達本身已有固定主語 it。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Treat It as an Ordinary Tense Exercise
rules.titleZh: 規則二：不要把它當作一般時態變化練習
rules.en: These forms might be created in a literal or highly unusual context, but they are not the familiar fixed saying taught here.
rules.zh: 在本練習中，不使用以上形式。 它們可能出現在字面或非常特殊的語境中，但並不是本課教授的常見固定說法。

rules.en: Changing the number usually creates a joke, parody or literal statement rather than the standard idiom.
rules.zh: 改變數字通常會變成笑話、仿作或字面陳述，而不再是標準慣用語。

rules.titleEn: Use It Only for a Truly Two-Sided Situation
rules.titleZh: 規則四：只用於真正涉及雙方的情況
rules.en: The situation is not meaningfully two-sided.
rules.zh: 兩位朋友都發出了傷人的訊息，卻互相指責。 一個巴掌拍不響。 如果只有一方作出錯誤行為，而另一方沒有參與，使用這個慣用語便不準確。

examples.en: It takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 兩位朋友都發出了傷人的訊息，卻互相指責。一個巴掌拍不響。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It to Blame a Victim
rules.titleZh: 規則五：不要用來責怪受害者
rules.en: abuse; harassment; bullying; threats; fraud; an attack; a serious power imbalance; a person who had no meaningful choice or participation. The saying should never be used automatically to suggest that every victim shares responsibility.
rules.zh: 在涉及虐待、騷擾、欺凌、威脅、詐騙、襲擊、嚴重權力不平等，或其中一方根本沒有選擇或參與的情況下，不應使用這個表達來分散責任。 不應自動使用這句話暗示每位受害者都需要承擔責任。

rules.titleEn: Shared Responsibility Does Not Always Mean
rules.titleZh: 規則六：雙方有責任不等於責任必定完全相等
rules.en: It does not scientifically calculate that each side is exactly fifty per cent responsible. The exercise uses clear situations in which both sides have made a meaningful contribution to the problem.
rules.zh: 這個表達通常表示雙方都對情況有所影響，但並不表示雙方的責任在所有情況下都必定完全相等。 本練習只使用雙方都明顯對問題有所影響的情境。

rules.titleZh: 規則七：分辨共同責任與共同合作
rules.en: Both uses share the same central idea: the situation cannot be explained or completed through only one side.
rules.zh: 兩名同事都隱瞞資料，令項目失敗； 雙方都有責任。 其中一個部門無法在另一個部門不參與的情況下完成共同項目； 事情需要雙方配合。 兩種用法的核心都相同：不能只從單方面解釋或完成整件事情。

examples.en: It takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 兩名同事都隱瞞資料，令項目失敗；雙方都有責任。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Full Meaning Unnecessarily
rules.titleZh: 規則八：不要不必要地重複完整意思
rules.en: The improved sentence lets the idiom carry the shared-responsibility meaning.
rules.zh: 任何一方都不應只責怪另一方； 一個巴掌拍不響。 改良句讓慣用語本身承擔「雙方都有責任」的意思。

examples.en: Neither person should blame the other alone; it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 任何一方都不應只責怪另一方；一個巴掌拍不響。

rules.en: the people; the relationship; the problem; the reason the saying is relevant.
rules.zh: 諾拉無法獨力修補與埃里克的友誼； 這需要雙方共同努力。 答案清楚保留了人物、關係、問題，以及慣用語適用的原因。

examples.en: Nora cannot repair her friendship with Eric alone—it takes two to tango.
examples.zh: 諾拉無法獨力修補與埃里克的友誼；這需要雙方共同努力。

rules.titleEn: “It Takes Two” Is Related but Excluded Here
rules.en: “It Takes Two” Is Related but Excluded Here
rules.zh: it takes two 是相關縮略形式，但本課不採用

instructions.zh: 使用以下表達改寫句子或完成回應：

questions.prompt: Leo blamed Sara for their argument, but he also shouted at her and refused to listen.
questions.promptZh: 里奧把爭吵歸咎於莎拉，但他也向她大叫，而且拒絕聆聽。
questions.answer: It takes two to tango; Leo should not place all the blame on Sara for their argument.
questions.answerZh: 一個巴掌拍不響；里奧不應把爭吵的全部責任推給莎拉。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: Nora wants to repair her friendship with Eric, but Eric refuses to speak to her. Her effort alone is not enough.
questions.promptZh: 諾拉希望修補與埃里克的友誼，但埃里克拒絕與她交談。單靠她一個人的努力並不足夠。
questions.answer: Nora cannot repair her friendship with Eric alone—it takes two to tango.
questions.answerZh: 諾拉無法獨力修補與埃里克的友誼；這需要雙方共同努力。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: The seller has accepted a lower price, but the buyer still refuses to sign. The seller cannot complete the deal alone.
questions.promptZh: 賣方已接受較低價格，但買方仍拒絕簽署。賣方無法獨力完成交易。
questions.answer: The seller’s effort alone cannot complete the deal with the buyer; it takes two to tango.
questions.answerZh: 單靠賣方的努力無法與買方完成交易；交易需要雙方同意。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: A: Red Club is ready to arrange the match. B: Blue Club must agree to the date as well.
questions.promptZh: 甲：紅隊已準備安排比賽。 乙：藍隊也必須同意比賽日期。
questions.answer: After all, it takes two to tango, so one club leader cannot arrange the match without the other.
questions.answerZh: 畢竟，事情需要雙方配合，因此其中一名球會領袖無法在另一人不同意的情況下安排比賽。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: Both neighbours shouted during the dispute, but everyone is blaming only Mr Lee.
questions.promptZh: 兩名鄰居在爭執期間都曾大叫，但所有人只責怪李先生。
questions.answer: Remember that it takes two to tango before blaming only Mr Lee for the dispute.
questions.answerZh: 在只責怪李先生之前，記住一個巴掌拍不響。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: Ava and Noah each failed to do their part of the project, but they are blaming each other.
questions.promptZh: 艾娃和諾亞都沒有完成自己負責的項目工作，但二人正在互相指責。
questions.answer: Neither Ava nor Noah should blame the other for their failed project; it takes two to tango.
questions.answerZh: 艾娃和諾亞都不應把項目失敗歸咎於對方；雙方都有責任。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: The teacher asked several questions, but the students remained silent. The teacher could not create a discussion alone.
questions.promptZh: 老師提出了幾條問題，但學生一直保持沉默。老師無法獨力帶動討論。
questions.answer: The teacher asked several questions, but the students remained silent; as the saying goes, it takes two to tango.
questions.answerZh: 老師提出了幾條問題，但學生一直保持沉默；正如俗語所說，事情需要雙方配合。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: One shop owner is doing all the work while the other rarely helps. The business cannot succeed this way.
questions.promptZh: 一名店主正在完成所有工作，另一名店主卻很少幫忙。生意無法以這種方式成功。
questions.answer: It takes two to tango, so the shop cannot succeed while one owner leaves all the work to the other.
questions.answerZh: 事情需要雙方配合，因此如果其中一名店主把所有工作留給另一人，店舖便無法成功。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: During the argument, both friends interrupted and insulted each other. Neither can honestly describe it as one-sided.
questions.promptZh: 爭吵期間，兩位朋友都曾打斷及侮辱對方。任何一方都不能誠實地說事情只是單方面造成的。
questions.answer: No one should pretend the argument was one-sided; when a conversation goes wrong, it takes two to tango.
questions.answerZh: 任何人都不應假裝這場爭吵只是單方面造成的；對話出現問題時，往往一個巴掌拍不響。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: The two players insulted each other after the match, but each blamed only the other. Their coach reminded them that both had contributed to the disagreement.
questions.promptZh: 兩名球員在比賽後互相侮辱，但每人都只責怪對方。教練提醒他們，兩人都對爭執有所影響。
questions.answer: “It takes two to tango,” the coach reminded the two players after their disagreement.
questions.answerZh: 兩名球員發生分歧後，教練提醒他們：「一個巴掌拍不響。」
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: Both teams missed important deadlines, but each team says the other caused the problem. The manager tells them to stop blaming each other.
questions.promptZh: 兩個團隊都錯過了重要限期，但每隊都表示問題由另一隊造成。經理要求他們停止互相指責。
questions.answer: The manager reminded both teams that it takes two to tango and asked them to stop blaming each other.
questions.answerZh: 經理提醒兩個團隊雙方都有責任，並要求他們停止互相指責。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: One team has offered to change several conditions, but the other team refuses to make any change. One team’s offer cannot secure the final agreement.
questions.promptZh: 一個團隊已提出更改幾項條件，但另一個團隊拒絕作出任何改變。單靠其中一隊的提議無法達成最終協議。
questions.answer: The offer from one team is not enough to secure the final agreement; put simply, it takes two to tango.
questions.answerZh: 單靠其中一隊提出改變，並不足以達成最終協議；簡單來說，協議需要雙方共同努力。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.

questions.prompt: A skilled mediator is helping two neighbours, but neither neighbour is willing to listen. The dispute is therefore continuing.
questions.promptZh: 一名經驗豐富的調解員正協助兩名鄰居，但任何一方都不願聆聽。因此，爭議仍在繼續。
questions.answer: Even with a skilled mediator, the dispute will continue if neither neighbour is willing to listen—it takes two to tango.
questions.answerZh: 即使有經驗豐富的調解員協助，如果兩名鄰居都不願聆聽，爭議仍會繼續；事情需要雙方配合。
questions.targetMeaning: 1. both people contributed to a disagreement or difficult situation; or 2. both people must be willing to take part for a shared activity, agreement or relationship to work.
